what_it_adds: Tech tiles, dreadnoughts, infiltrate, CHOAM/freighter track, Epic game mode and 6 new leaders.
what_it_fixes: Base game openings can feel samey (spice-for-solari rush); adds new paths to win.
verdict_reason: Most BGG thread replies picked it as the one to get first: new leaders and tech tiles open up more varied opening strategies.
notes: First expansion (late 2021, Wikipedia). Wikipedia says Uprising is compatible with Rise of Ix. Verdict rests on one BGG thread.

what_it_adds: Bene Tleilax board, research station, grafting of cards.
what_it_fixes: Makes deck-building matter more, with new ways to improve and trim your deck.
verdict_reason: Good pick if your group wants a stronger deck-building side; some BGG players prefer it over Rise of Ix.
notes: Second expansion (late 2022, Wikipedia). Needs 57 extra sleeves if you sleeve. Wikipedia says Uprising is compatible with Immortality. ASIN from amazon.com/dp link on https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3038797/first-expansion-to-buy-rise-of-ix-or-immortality.

requires_also: Dune: Imperium or Dune: Imperium – Uprising
what_it_adds: Sardaukar commanders with skill tiles, tech tiles, 9 leaders, 32 Imperium and 18 intrigue cards, contracts.
what_it_fixes: Tech tiles are easier to buy than in Rise of Ix (any green space).
verdict_reason: Reviewers call it excellent with Uprising, but mixing it into the original game plus older expansions gets messy. Best if you own or plan to get Uprising.
notes: Works with both Dune: Imperium and Uprising. US retail Jan 27, 2025. Gideon plays 1-4. ASIN from amzn.to link on https://gideonsgaming.com/dune-imperium-bloodlines-review/.

what_it_adds: Spies, sandworms, nine leaders and a six-player team mode.
what_it_fixes: Combat is more decisive, driven by sandworms (Polygon).
verdict_reason: It is a standalone replacement, not an add-on: reviewers rate it better than the original, but you are buying a second full game. Get it if you want the newer version; skip it if base plus Rise of Ix already suits you.
notes: STANDALONE game (Wikipedia: replacement for or alternative to the original); listed here so owners see it. Polygon: compatible with existing expansions, includes 6-player mode. Min players not verified.

what_it_adds: Extended 4-season board, structure cards and special workers.
what_it_fixes: Spring and fall get real actions, and a new trade action gives more flexible turns.
verdict_reason: Reviewers call it a must-have for Viticulture fans: a four-season board, new actions and more choices without much extra time.
notes: Only AUD price shown ($54 AUD). Original Tuscany owners already have this content. 2p variant without influence map. ASIN from amazon.com/dp link on https://www.geeksundergrace.com/tabletop/review-tuscany-essential-edition/. What Board Game (Bordeaux review) still calls Tuscany the better expansion.

what_it_adds: 40 new visitor cards; no overlap with base cards.
what_it_fixes: More visitor variety with no extra rules.
verdict_reason: Cheap, shuffles straight into the base decks and adds variety with no extra rules. Not essential, but fans rarely take it back out.
notes: Works with any Viticulture version. Only AUD price shown ($25 AUD). Do not mix with Rhine Valley visitors. Designer uses Moor at higher player counts. Verdict rests on one independent review.

what_it_adds: Cooperative mode across 7 continents, with solo mode.
verdict_reason: A hard co-op mode where every player must reach 25 points in six years. Meeple Mountain says it is for strong Viticulture players only; new players should learn the base game first.
notes: Retail July 22, 2022 (publisher). Publisher suggests new players play base first. Hard; difficulty variants exist. ASIN from amazon.com/dp link on https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/viticulture-world-cooperative-expansion/.

what_it_adds: Alt 4-season board, experts, trade market, face-up cards, end-game conversion.
what_it_fixes: Design goals: faster start and better 2-player game (publisher).
verdict_reason: A new four-season board that speeds up the start and pushes you toward making wine. What Board Game still rates Tuscany higher, so it matters most if you do not own Tuscany.
notes: Only AUD price shown ($33 AUD). Local retail Feb 27, 2026; online Mar 13, 2026. Not compatible with Viticulture World board (WBG). Verdict rests on one independent review.

prerequisite_rule: You need Viticulture. It replaces all your other visitor cards, and 4 of its cards also need Tuscany.
what_it_adds: Alternate set of 80 visitor cards focused on the wine business, not points.
verdict_reason: Good if your group wants visitor cards that build your wine business instead of handing out points. It replaces your other visitor cards, so it is a different flavour, not more game.
notes: 2026-09-29: Stonemaier US store $17 (compare-at $20). Replaces all other visitor cards; do not mix with base, Tuscany or Moor visitors. 4 cards need Tuscany; 6 duplicate existing cards. Reviewers split vs Moor Visitors.

what_it_adds: Two-sided board, 36 cards, market board, flooded caverns and swimming.
what_it_fixes: Adds a new double-sided map and simple flooded-room rules for fresh variety.
verdict_reason: Meeple Mountain preferred it over Mummy's Curse, and several BGG players said: if you get one, get this.

what_it_adds: Two-sided board, 41 cards, a wandering mummy and pyramid die.
what_it_fixes: Adds a new map and card set for more replay value.
verdict_reason: Fun new map and cards, but Meeple Mountain found the mummy rarely does much, so it ranks behind Sunken Treasures.

what_it_adds: Double-sided board: Dwarven Mine and Spider Queen's Lair, with tokens and a market board; no new cards.
what_it_fixes: Two maps with their own simple rules add variety.
verdict_reason: Reviewers found both maps easy to teach and different enough to change how you play; the only gripe is no new cards.

expansion_name: Clank! Expeditions: Temple of the Ape Lords
what_it_adds: New boards in the Expeditions series.
what_it_fixes: New map where the paths change, plus a short campaign option.
verdict_reason: BGG players rank it just after Sunken Treasures; its shifting paths and mini-campaign are liked.
notes: Only one BGG thread supports the verdict; contents not verified beyond Dire Wolf shop listing.

what_it_adds: 6 asymmetric starting decks/characters and a side board for 5-6 players.
what_it_fixes: Lets 5-6 people play and gives each player different starting powers.
verdict_reason: Get it if you want 5-6 players or unique player decks; BGG players note it adds no new maps and can feel fiddly.

what_it_adds: Landmarks with end-game bonuses, more wildlife scoring cards and habitat tiles, 5-6 player parts.
what_it_fixes: Adds 6th-player support and landmark goals that reward big habitat groups.
complexity_change: Deeper without many new mechanisms (reviewer quotes on publisher page).
verdict_reason: Meeple Mountain rates it great for people who already love Cascadia, but not needed for your first games.
notes: Publisher page quotes are curated; verdict rests on one independent review (Meeple Mountain). ASIN from amazon.com/dp link on https://www.meeplemountain.com/reviews/cascadia-landmarks/.
